native.admission_inspect: Pearl, cut thin as a compliment. One face is blank. The other flatters you in a hand too even to be kind.
apply_texts: Another reading, no less polished. The card offers beauty without amendment, and you almost thank it.
Held too long, the compliment cools. It still flatters the pose, and the face that misses it feels the draft.
The card repeats its kindness. This time the words fit a better version of you, and the gap is not polite.
The flattery is unchanged. What changes is the pause before you believe it, and that pause is not free.
The last compliment arrives flawless and unspent. You wear it anyway. Nothing in the room improves.
The praise is exquisite and does not take. The pearl stays bright; you do not feel correspondingly arranged.
You accept the card's praise. For a moment your reflection agrees, which is the cheapest form of mercy.
You accept the praise, and notice the pearl is warmer where a thumb would rest. No thumb has rested there.
You turn the bright face toward yourself. The compliment is immaculate, and it declines to recognize you.
You turn the card again. The same perfect line returns late, and leaves a small, fashionable chill.
inspect_texts: A calling-card of pearl, unused and too smooth. One edge is warmer than the rest, though nothing has held it.
Blank on one face, over-finished on the other. The same praise sits there, as if repetition could pass for regard.
Pearl, cut thin as a compliment. One face is blank. The other flatters you in a hand too even to be kind.
The card is lovely and slightly cold. Its praise fits your posture better than your face, and will not smudge.
The pearl card waits with its last compliment already composed. The lettering is perfect, and a fraction late.
The pearl has not dulled. Only the compliment has: still elegant, and no longer willing to meet your eye.
native.name: Even Pearl Card
